Question 8773. How many cervical vertebrae are there in the normal spine: 5, 6, 7, or 8? The answer is 7. They lie between the skull above and the thoracic vertebrae below. The seventh has a long spine that can be felt at the base of the neck.

Question 8774. Which cervical vertebra carries the peg-like dens, the pivot around which the head turns: the atlas, the axis, the seventh cervical vertebra, or the first thoracic vertebra? The answer is the axis, the second cervical vertebra. The dens projects upward from its body and is held against the front of the atlas by a ligament.

Question 8775. Through which part of a cervical vertebra does the vertebral artery pass: the vertebral foramen, the transverse foramen, the intervertebral foramen, or the foramen magnum? The answer is the transverse foramen, in the transverse process. The artery runs up through these foramina from the sixth vertebra to the first. The vertebral foramen carries the spinal cord.

Question 8776. A described radiograph taken through the open mouth shows two rounded masses on either side of the upper cervical spine with a small peg of bone standing between them. Which part of which bone is the peg? The answer is the dens of the axis. The two masses are the lateral masses of the atlas.

Question 8777. Which structure lies immediately behind the dens of the axis, so that it is at risk when the dens is displaced backward? The answer is the spinal cord, in the vertebral canal. The transverse ligament of the atlas holds the dens against the anterior arch of the atlas. If the dens breaks or the ligament tears, the cord can be compressed.

Question 8778. A constructed illustration: after a fall on the head, a person has pain in the neck, and the peg of the second cervical vertebra is seen to be displaced backward on a described radiograph. Which structure is in danger of compression? The answer is the spinal cord, which lies just behind the dens. The upper cervical cord also carries the fibers that supply the diaphragm.

Question 8779. Which of these pairs belongs together: the atlanto-occipital joint with rotation of the head, the atlantoaxial joint with nodding, the atlantoaxial joint with rotation, or the atlanto-occipital joint with side bending only? The answer is the atlantoaxial joint with rotation, which turns the head to look to one side. Nodding takes place mainly at the atlanto-occipital joint.

Question 8780. Name the two cervical vertebrae that are atypical in shape, and say briefly what makes each one different, spoken as a list. The answer is the atlas and the axis. The atlas has no body and no spine, and the axis carries the dens. Both take part in the movements of the head.

Question 8781. Which plexus of nerves lies in the posterior triangle of the neck and supplies the skin of the neck and of the shoulder? The answer is the cervical plexus. It is formed by the first four cervical nerves. Its branches wind around the middle of the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

Question 8782. Which structures emerge from between the anterior and the middle scalene muscles, together with the subclavian artery? The answer is the trunks of the brachial plexus. The upper and the middle trunks lie above the artery and the lower trunk behind it. The plexus then passes under the clavicle into the axilla.

Question 8783. Which of these nerves arises from the cervical plexus: the phrenic nerve, the accessory nerve, the hypoglossal nerve, or the vagus nerve? The answer is the phrenic nerve, from the third, fourth and fifth cervical nerves. The accessory nerve is a cranial nerve that enters the neck through the jugular foramen. The vagus also leaves the skull through the jugular foramen.

Question 8784. Which muscle of the shoulder is supplied by the accessory nerve: the trapezius, the levator scapulae, the rhomboid major, or the serratus anterior? The answer is the trapezius. The accessory nerve also supplies the sternocleidomastoid. The other three muscles are supplied by branches of the cervical and the brachial plexuses.

Question 8785. Into which vein does the thoracic duct usually empty: the left subclavian vein at the left venous angle, the right subclavian vein, the superior vena cava, or the azygos vein? The answer is the left venous angle. It drains the lower limbs, the abdomen and the left side of the head, the neck and the chest. The right lymphatic duct drains the rest.

Question 8786. A described dissection of the root of the neck shows a thin-walled vessel arching laterally across the front of the vertebral artery and ending at the junction of two large veins. Which vessel is shown? The answer is the thoracic duct. It ends at the left venous angle. Its thin wall and pale color distinguish it from the arteries around it.

Question 8787. The sympathetic trunk in the neck lies immediately in front of which muscles, and behind which layer of fascia? The answer is the longus colli and the longus capitis, behind the prevertebral fascia. It also lies behind the carotid sheath. Its ganglia supply the head and the neck.

Question 8788. A constructed illustration: a person has a drooping upper eyelid, a small pupil and no sweating on one side of the face, while the eye itself moves normally. Which structure is involved? The answer is the sympathetic trunk in the neck, and the eye movements are normal because the third, fourth and sixth cranial nerves are not affected. The pattern is described as Horner syndrome.

Question 8789. Which of these pairs belongs together: the internal jugular vein with the carotid sheath, the external jugular vein with the carotid sheath, the thoracic duct with the right venous angle, or the accessory nerve with the anterior triangle? The answer is the internal jugular vein with the carotid sheath. The external jugular vein lies outside the sheath, and the thoracic duct ends at the left venous angle.

Question 8790. True or false: the phrenic nerve lies on the anterior surface of the anterior scalene muscle, while the trunks of the brachial plexus lie between the anterior and the middle scalene muscles. The answer is true. The subclavian artery also passes between the two scalene muscles, behind the plexus.

Question 8791. Which layer of the scalp lies between the fibrous sheet of the galea and the periosteum of the skull, and allows infection to spread widely? The answer is the loose areolar layer, the fourth layer of the scalp. It contains the small veins that connect the scalp with the intracranial venous sinuses. Because it is loose, pus and blood spread easily through it.

Question 8792. Which layer of the scalp holds the arteries, the veins and the nerves of the scalp, and why does a cut through it gape and bleed heavily? The answer is the connective tissue layer, the second layer of the scalp. Its fibrous bands hold the walls of the vessels open when they are cut.

Question 8793. Which of these muscles closes the eye: the orbicularis oculi, the orbicularis oris, the buccinator, or the platysma? The answer is the orbicularis oculi. It encircles the orbit and is supplied by the facial nerve. The orbicularis oris closes the lips, and the buccinator presses the cheek against the teeth.

Question 8794. Which branch of the facial nerve is at greatest risk during an operation on the submandibular gland: the temporal branch, the zygomatic branch, the marginal mandibular branch, or the cervical branch? The answer is the marginal mandibular branch. It runs forward below the angle and the lower border of the mandible. Injury weakens the muscles that pull down the corner of the mouth.

Question 8795. Which of these findings points to a lesion of the facial nerve rather than to a lesion of the trigeminal nerve: loss of taste on the front two thirds of the tongue, loss of sensation over the forehead, weakness of the masseter, or numbness of the chin? The answer is loss of taste on the front two thirds of the tongue, carried by the chorda tympani. The other findings all belong to the trigeminal nerve.

Question 8796. A described dissection shows a thin sheet of muscle arising from the fascia over the chest and running up over the jaw to the corner of the mouth and the lower lip. Which muscle is shown? The answer is the platysma, supplied by the cervical branch of the facial nerve. It lies in the superficial fascia of the neck and tenses the skin of the neck.

Question 8797. Which venous plexus lies in the infratemporal fossa around the muscles of mastication and communicates with the cavernous sinus through small veins? The answer is the pterygoid venous plexus. It drains the deep parts of the face and connects with the facial vein. That connection is one route by which facial infection reaches the cavernous sinus.

Question 8798. A constructed illustration: a person is struck on the temple, recovers briefly, and then becomes deeply drowsy; a described scan shows a lens-shaped collection of blood between the skull and the dura. Which artery has bled? The answer is the middle meningeal artery, torn where the bones of the pterion meet. The sutures limit the spread of the blood, so it forms a lens.

Question 8799. True or false: the facial nerve supplies the muscles of mastication. The answer is false. The muscles of mastication, the masseter, the temporalis and the two pterygoids, are supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. The facial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression, including the platysma and the stapedius.

Question 8800. Name the five groups of branches into which the facial nerve divides inside the parotid gland, spoken as a list. The answer is the temporal, the zygomatic, the buccal, the marginal mandibular and the cervical branches. They fan out across the side of the face. Injury to the marginal mandibular branch weakens the lower lip.

To summarize, the base of the skull is a map of openings, with the cribriform plate for the fibers of smell, the optic canal for the optic nerve, the superior orbital fissure for the third, fourth and sixth cranial nerves and the first division of the trigeminal nerve, the foramen rotundum for the maxillary nerve, the foramen ovale for the mandibular nerve, the foramen spinosum for the middle meningeal artery, the internal acoustic meatus for the facial and the vestibulocochlear nerves, the jugular foramen for the glossopharyngeal, the vagus and the accessory nerves, and the hypoglossal canal for the twelfth cranial nerve. The orbit, the nose and the paranasal sinuses drain by fixed routes, with the maxillary and the frontal sinuses opening into the middle meatus and the nasolacrimal duct into the inferior meatus, while the cavernous sinus holds the internal carotid artery and the abducens nerve within its cavity. The mouth and the larynx turn on nerves that must be named exactly, the lingual nerve for sensation and the chorda tympani for taste in the front of the tongue, the hypoglossal nerve for the tongue muscles, the recurrent laryngeal nerve for all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid, and the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve for that one exception. The neck is organized by the sternocleidomastoid muscle into an anterior and a posterior triangle, with the carotid sheath in front of the prevertebral muscles, the accessory nerve crossing the posterior triangle, and the thoracic duct ending at the left venous angle. This chapter is educational material and does not replace an anatomy course, a dissection, a clinical training program, or the judgment of a teacher.

# Chapter 89 — Head and Neck, Part Two

The head and the neck carry the face, the jaws, the salivary glands, the tongue and the spaces between them, and above the diaphragm the thorax holds the lungs, the heart and the great vessels. This chapter works through the muscles of the face and of chewing, the temporomandibular joint, the tongue and the pharynx, the root of the neck with its vessels and its nerves, and then the chest wall, the pleura, the lungs, the mediastinum and the heart. It holds one hundred questions, and every one gives its answer at once and then explains why, so nothing has to be held in mind until the end. This is educational material, and it supports rather than replaces an anatomy course, a dissection, a clinical training program, or the judgment of a teacher.

Question 8801. Which muscle forms a complete ring around the mouth and closes the lips? The answer is the orbicularis oris. Its fibers circle the opening of the mouth and blend with the muscles that radiate toward it. It is supplied by the facial nerve.

Question 8802. Which muscle of the face runs from the cheekbone to the angle of the mouth and lifts that angle when a person smiles? The answer is the zygomaticus major. It arises from the zygomatic bone and passes downward and forward to the corner of the mouth. A weak muscle on one side flattens that smile.

Question 8803. Which nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression: the trigeminal nerve, the facial nerve, the hypoglossal nerve, or the glossopharyngeal nerve? The answer is the facial nerve. It leaves the skull through the stylomastoid foramen and fans out within the parotid gland. The trigeminal nerve supplies the muscles of chewing instead.

Question 8804. A described dissection of the cheek shows a sheet of muscle running from the back of the mouth to the angle of the mouth, with a duct piercing it to open opposite the upper second molar tooth. Which structures are described? The answer is the buccinator muscle and the parotid duct. The buccinator keeps food between the teeth, and the duct carries saliva from the gland.

Question 8805. Which structure lies inside the parotid gland and divides it into a superficial and a deep part? The answer is the facial nerve with its branches. The nerve enters the gland behind the jaw and spreads through it in a fan. The external carotid artery and the retromandibular vein also lie within the gland, but the nerve separates the two parts.

Question 8806. Which muscle of chewing lies in the space behind the upper jaw and pulls the lower jaw forward: the temporalis, the masseter, the medial pterygoid, or the lateral pterygoid? The answer is the lateral pterygoid. It runs from the base of the skull to the neck of the mandible. It is the only muscle of chewing that protrudes the jaw, and it also helps to open the mouth.

Question 8807. Which fan-shaped muscle fills the hollow above the ear and raises the lower jaw, with its tendon passing deep to the cheekbone? The answer is the temporalis. Its tendon passes behind the zygomatic arch and inserts on the coronoid process. It also retracts a jaw that has been pushed forward.

Question 8808. True or false: the muscles of chewing are supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. The answer is true. That division leaves the skull through the foramen ovale and supplies the masseter, the temporalis and both pterygoid muscles. The same division also carries sensation from the lower teeth and the chin.

Question 8809. A constructed illustration: after a deep cut in front of the left ear, the left side of the face does not move, the left eye will not close, and only the right side of the forehead creases. Which nerve has been divided? The answer is the left facial nerve, before it divides inside the gland. Its branches supply every muscle of facial expression there.

Question 8810. Through which opening does the space behind the upper jaw communicate with the orbit: the superior orbital fissure, the inferior orbital fissure, the foramen rotundum, or the foramen ovale? The answer is the inferior orbital fissure. It lies between the floor and the lateral wall of the orbit. The maxillary nerve and the inferior ophthalmic veins pass through it.

Question 8811. Which of these pairs belongs together: the chorda tympani with the submandibular ganglion, the greater petrosal nerve with the submandibular ganglion, the lesser petrosal nerve with the ciliary ganglion, or the nasociliary nerve with the pterygopalatine ganglion? The answer is the chorda tympani with the submandibular ganglion. It carries taste from the front of the tongue and joins the lingual nerve.

Question 8812. Which gland lies in the floor of the mouth, wraps around the back of the mylohyoid muscle, and opens by a duct beside the frenulum of the tongue? The answer is the submandibular gland. Its duct runs forward under the lining of the mouth. The sublingual gland lies beside it and opens by several small ducts.

Question 8813. Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of the tongue: the trigeminal nerve, the facial nerve, the hypoglossal nerve, or the vagus nerve? The answer is the hypoglossal nerve. It leaves the skull through the hypoglossal canal and runs to the tongue. It supplies every muscle of the tongue except the palatoglossus, which the vagus nerve reaches.

Question 8814. A described cross section of the neck shows a tube of cartilage in the midline, a flat gland wrapped around its front and sides, and two small rounded bodies set in the back of that gland. Which structures are described? The answer is the larynx and the trachea, the thyroid gland, and the parathyroid glands. The parathyroids usually lie on the back of the thyroid gland.

Question 8815. Which structure lies immediately in front of the ear, deep to the skin, and can be felt pulsating over the root of the zygomatic arch? The answer is the superficial temporal artery. It is one of the two terminal branches of the external carotid artery. It ascends across the temple and divides into a frontal and a parietal branch.

Question 8816. A constructed illustration: a stab wound in the posterior triangle of the neck is followed by a drooping shoulder and weakness in shrugging that shoulder. Which nerve has been injured? The answer is the accessory nerve. It crosses the posterior triangle on its way to the trapezius muscle. That muscle therefore loses its main nerve supply.

Question 8817. Name three structures that lie within the carotid sheath in the neck. The answer is the common carotid artery and its continuation, the internal jugular vein, and the vagus nerve. The sheath runs from the base of the skull to the root of the neck. The vein lies lateral to the artery, and the nerve lies behind and between them.

Question 8818. Which statement about the thoracic duct is correct: it ends at the left venous angle, it ends at the right venous angle, it ends at the arch of the aorta, or it ends at the azygos vein? The answer is that it ends at the left venous angle. That angle is where the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins meet. The right lymphatic duct ends at the right venous angle.

Question 8819. Which trunk arises from the first part of the subclavian artery and gives off the inferior thyroid, the suprascapular and the transverse cervical arteries? The answer is the thyrocervical trunk. It arises just medial to the scalenus anterior muscle. The inferior thyroid artery supplies the lower part of the thyroid gland.

Question 8820. A described radiograph of the side of the head shows the lower jaw with two processes at its upper end, separated by a notch, and the rounded head of the jaw in a hollow in front of the ear. Which structures are described? The answer is the coronoid process, the condylar process and the temporomandibular joint. The notch between them is the mandibular notch.

Question 8821. Which statement about the temporomandibular joint is correct: it is divided into two compartments by a disc, it is a simple hinge with one cavity, it has no fibrous capsule, or its two sides move independently? The answer is that it is divided into two compartments by a fibrocartilaginous disc. The lower compartment allows the hinge movement, and the upper allows the jaw to glide.

Question 8822. The hyoid bone, the thyroid cartilage and the cricoid cartilage lie one below another in the neck. In which plane do all three lie, and in which plane would all three be seen from the side? The answer is the median plane, and a sagittal plane would show them from the side. All three lie in the midline.

Question 8823. Which cartilage of the larynx forms a complete ring and is felt as a firm rounded prominence below the thyroid cartilage? The answer is the cricoid cartilage. It is the only complete ring in the airway and lies below the thyroid cartilage. The first ring of the trachea begins beneath it.

Question 8824. Which nerve ascends in the groove between the trachea and the esophagus to reach the larynx? The answer is the recurrent laryngeal nerve. On the right it hooks around the right subclavian artery, and on the left around the arch of the aorta. It supplies all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid.

Question 8825. The recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except which one: the cricothyroid, the thyroarytenoid, the posterior cricoarytenoid, or the lateral cricoarytenoid? The answer is the cricothyroid. It is supplied by the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. The posterior cricoarytenoid is the only muscle that opens the vocal folds.

Question 8826. A constructed illustration: after an operation in the lower neck, a person has a hoarse voice and the left vocal fold lies near the midline. Which nerve was injured, and why is the left one more exposed? The answer is the left recurrent laryngeal nerve, which hooks around the arch of the aorta and has a much longer course than the right. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8827. A described specimen shows the tongue drawn forward, with a fold of lining running from the side of the tongue to the wall of the pharynx, and a small mass of lymphoid tissue behind that fold. Which structures are described? The answer is the palatoglossal fold and the palatine tonsil. The fold forms the anterior pillar of the fauces, in front of the tonsil.

Question 8828. Which pair belongs together: the temporalis with the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve, the orbicularis oculi with the mandibular division, the lateral pterygoid with the facial nerve, or the front belly of the digastric with the hypoglossal nerve? The answer is the temporalis with the mandibular division. That division supplies every muscle of chewing and also the front belly of the digastric.

Question 8829. Which of these arteries is a branch of the external carotid artery: the maxillary artery, the ophthalmic artery, the vertebral artery, or the thyrocervical trunk? The answer is the maxillary artery. It is one of the two terminal branches of the external carotid artery. The ophthalmic artery arises from the internal carotid artery.

Question 8830. Which bone forms the lower jaw, carries the lower teeth, and joins the skull at a joint in front of each ear? The answer is the mandible. It has a body that carries the teeth and two ascending rami. Each ramus ends above in a coronoid process and a condyle, which forms the joint.

Question 8831. True or false: the maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve leaves the skull through the foramen ovale. The answer is false. It leaves through the foramen rotundum. The foramen ovale carries the mandibular division. The maxillary division carries sensation from the upper teeth, the cheek and the upper lip.

Question 8832. Which muscle forms the floor of the mouth and is supplied by a branch of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve: the mylohyoid, the geniohyoid, the stylohyoid, or the thyrohyoid? The answer is the mylohyoid. It runs from the mandible to the hyoid bone and supports the tongue. The geniohyoid and the thyrohyoid are supplied by the first cervical nerve.

Question 8833. A described dissection of the root of the neck shows three trunks formed between the anterior and the middle scalene muscles. Which structure is described? The answer is the brachial plexus. The trunks are the upper, the middle and the lower. The subclavian artery also passes between those muscles, in front of the trunks.

Question 8834. Which vein lies immediately in front of the subclavian artery at the root of the neck, separated from it by the scalenus anterior muscle? The answer is the subclavian vein. It lies between the clavicle and the first rib, in front of that muscle. The phrenic nerve crosses the front of the muscle and passes behind the vein.

Question 8835. Which sympathetic ganglion in the neck is the largest, lies at the level of the second and third cervical vertebrae, and gives off the superior cardiac nerve? The answer is the superior cervical ganglion. It lies behind the carotid sheath and in front of the prevertebral fascia. The middle ganglion is the smallest, at the level of the cricoid cartilage.

Question 8836. A constructed illustration: a person has a drooping upper eyelid, a small pupil and a dry flushed face after a deep injury in the neck. Which part of the nervous system has been damaged? The answer is the sympathetic chain in the neck. Its fibers reach the eye and the sweat glands of the face. Interruption of that pathway produces these signs.

Question 8837. Which fascial space of the neck lies behind the pharynx and the esophagus, in front of the prevertebral fascia, and continues downward into the chest? The answer is the retropharyngeal space. It runs from the base of the skull to the upper part of the posterior mediastinum. Because it is continuous with the chest, infection can travel along it.

Question 8838. Which pair belongs together: the sternocleidomastoid with the accessory nerve, the trapezius with the thoracodorsal nerve, the rhomboid muscles with the axillary nerve, or the levator scapulae with the suprascapular nerve? The answer is the sternocleidomastoid with the accessory nerve, which also supplies the trapezius. The thoracodorsal nerve supplies the latissimus dorsi, and the dorsal scapular nerve supplies the rhomboids.

Question 8839. Which muscle of the neck has one head on the manubrium of the sternum and one on the medial part of the clavicle, and divides the neck into an anterior and a posterior triangle? The answer is the sternocleidomastoid. It runs upward and backward to the mastoid process. Turning the head to the opposite side makes it stand out.

Question 8840. Which of these structures lies in the triangle bounded by the two bellies of the digastric muscle and the lower border of the mandible: the submandibular gland, the accessory nerve, the phrenic nerve, or the brachial plexus? The answer is the submandibular gland. It fills that triangle and wraps around the mylohyoid muscle. The other three lie elsewhere.

Question 8841. A described dissection of the cheek shows a pad of fat lying between the buccinator and the masseter, with a fan of nerve branches spreading over it. Which structures are described? The answer is the buccal fat pad and the branches of the facial nerve. The pad separates the muscles and is prominent in a newborn.

Question 8842. Which statement about the muscles of the soft palate is correct: the tensor veli palatini is supplied by the mandibular division, the levator veli palatini by the facial nerve, the palatoglossus by the hypoglossal nerve, or the uvular muscle by the glossopharyngeal nerve? The answer is that the tensor veli palatini is supplied by the mandibular division. The remaining muscles of the palate are supplied through the pharyngeal plexus.

Question 8843. Which nerve descends on the front of the scalenus anterior muscle, behind the prevertebral fascia, and continues through the chest to the diaphragm? The answer is the phrenic nerve. It is formed mainly from the fourth cervical nerve, with a contribution from the third and the fifth. In the neck it lies lateral to the vagus nerve and in front of the subclavian artery.

Question 8844. Which muscle has a front belly from the chin to the hyoid bone and a back belly from the mastoid process to the hyoid, with a tendon between them? The answer is the digastric muscle. The front belly is supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve, and the back belly by the facial nerve. Together they raise the hyoid bone.

Question 8845. A constructed illustration: bleeding begins from the lower part of the tonsillar bed during an operation in the throat, and the artery there must be named. Which artery is it? The answer is the tonsillar branch of the facial artery. The facial artery winds over the jaw and gives that branch near the back of the tongue. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8846. Which artery crosses the lower border of the mandible in front of the masseter muscle and continues upward toward the angle of the mouth? The answer is the facial artery. It is a branch of the external carotid artery and grooves the submandibular gland as it turns around the jaw. Its pulse can be felt where it crosses the bone.

Question 8847. A described specimen of the larynx is opened from behind and shows two folds running from front to back on each side, with a space between them. Which structures are described? The answer is the vestibular fold above and the vocal fold below, with the ventricle of the larynx between them. The vocal fold contains the vocal ligament.

Question 8848. Which statement about the nerves of the tongue is correct: taste from the front of the tongue travels through the facial nerve and general sensation through the trigeminal nerve, taste from the front travels with the hypoglossal nerve, sensation from the back travels with the facial nerve, or all sensation travels with the glossopharyngeal nerve? The answer is the first statement. Taste from the back of the tongue travels with the glossopharyngeal nerve.

Question 8849. A described dissection of the floor of the mouth shows a thin sheet of muscle stretched between the two halves of the jaw, with a duct and a nerve running above it. Which structures lie above that sheet? The answer is the submandibular duct and the lingual nerve. The duct opens beside the frenulum, and the lingual nerve carries sensation and taste.

Question 8850. Through which opening does the facial nerve leave the skull: the stylomastoid foramen, the jugular foramen, the foramen ovale, or the internal acoustic meatus? The answer is the stylomastoid foramen. The nerve enters the skull at the internal acoustic meatus and leaves at the stylomastoid foramen, just behind the styloid process. It then enters the parotid gland.

Question 8851. Which dome-shaped muscle separates the chest from the abdomen and is the chief muscle of breathing? The answer is the diaphragm. It arises from the lower ribs, the back of the sternum and the upper lumbar vertebrae, and its fibers converge on a central tendon. When it contracts, it flattens and draws air into the lungs.

Question 8852. Which of these structures passes through the aortic opening of the diaphragm: the aorta, the inferior vena cava, the esophagus, or the right phrenic nerve? The answer is the aorta. The thoracic duct and the azygos vein pass through the same opening beside it. The opening lies at the level of the twelfth thoracic vertebra.

Question 8853. Which opening in the diaphragm lies in the central tendon, at the level of the eighth thoracic vertebra, and carries the inferior vena cava? The answer is the caval opening. It lies a little to the right of the midline, and the right phrenic nerve pierces the muscle beside it. The opening admits the widest of the three main channels.

Question 8854. A described frontal radiograph of the chest shows a dark area on each side crossed by faint curved lines, and a dense shadow in the middle. Which structures are shown? The answer is the two lungs with the ribs crossing them, and the heart with the mediastinum between. The diaphragm forms the curved lower border.

Question 8855. Which nerves supply the diaphragm: the intercostal nerves alone, the phrenic nerves with the lower intercostal nerves, the vagus nerves, or the sympathetic trunk? The answer is the phrenic nerves with the lower intercostal nerves. The phrenic nerves carry the motor supply, and the lower intercostal nerves carry sensation from the outer rim. Irritation can therefore refer pain to the shoulder.

Question 8856. Which structure lies immediately behind the sternum in the chest of a child, and what becomes of it in adult life? The answer is the thymus, which shrinks and is replaced largely by fat. It lies in the anterior mediastinum in front of the heart and the great vessels. It is largest in early childhood.

Question 8857. Which serous membrane lines the inside of the chest wall and covers the surface of each lung: the pleura, the pericardium, the peritoneum, or the endothoracic fascia? The answer is the pleura. The parietal layer lines the wall, and the visceral layer is stuck to the lung. The film of fluid between them lets the layers slide as the lung moves.

Question 8858. True or false: the lowest part of the pleural sac on each side is not filled by lung, even in full inspiration. The answer is true. That part is the costodiaphragmatic recess, between the lower border of the lung and the diaphragm. It fills with fluid when the pleural cavity is inflamed.

Question 8859. Which of these structures lies in the posterior mediastinum: the thoracic duct, the phrenic nerve, the thymus, or the arch of the aorta? The answer is the thoracic duct. It ascends in front of the vertebral column, behind the esophagus, and to the left of the midline. The phrenic nerve and the thymus lie further forward.

Question 8860. A constructed illustration: after a broken rib, air enters the space around a lung and the lung shrinks away from the chest wall. Which space has the air entered, and what are its two layers? The answer is the pleural cavity, between the parietal pleura and the visceral pleura. It normally holds only a thin film of fluid.

Question 8861. Which fissure separates the upper lobe of the right lung from the middle lobe: the horizontal fissure, the oblique fissure, the azygos fissure, or the superior accessory fissure? The answer is the horizontal fissure. It runs forward from the oblique fissure at the level of the fourth costal cartilage. The left lung has no horizontal fissure, because it has only two lobes.

Question 8862. Which of these statements about the left lung is correct: it has two lobes with a cardiac notch and a lingula, it has three lobes with a horizontal fissure, it has two lobes with a horizontal fissure, or it has four lobes? The answer is that it has two lobes, with a cardiac notch and a lingula. The notch is where the heart presses on the lung.

Question 8863. A described cross section of the chest at the level of the sternal angle shows a large vessel crossing in front of the windpipe and passing backward to its left. Which vessel is described? The answer is the arch of the aorta. It begins behind the sternal angle and curves over the left main bronchus. The trachea divides beneath it.

Question 8864. Which structure lies immediately behind the left atrium of the heart and in front of the vertebral column? The answer is the esophagus, with the descending aorta to its left. The esophagus passes down through the posterior mediastinum and pierces the diaphragm. The left atrium therefore lies in front of it.

Question 8865. Which chamber of the heart forms the apex, pointing downward, forward and to the left? The answer is the left ventricle. Its wall is the thickest of the four chambers because it pumps blood around the whole body. The right ventricle forms most of the front of the heart instead.

Question 8866. Which valve guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle, and how many cusps does it have: the mitral valve, the tricuspid valve, the aortic valve, or the pulmonary valve? The answer is the tricuspid valve, which has three cusps. The mitral valve lies on the left side of the heart and has two cusps.

Question 8867. Name the two coronary arteries and the branch of the left one that runs down the front of the heart in the groove between the two ventricles. The answer is the right and the left coronary arteries, with the anterior interventricular branch of the left. The right coronary artery usually supplies the back of the heart.

Question 8868. A constructed illustration: a person feels a tearing pain between the shoulder blades, and imaging shows a split in the wall of the aorta beyond the origin of the left subclavian artery. Which part of the aorta is involved? The answer is the descending thoracic aorta. It continues downward in the posterior mediastinum to the diaphragm. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8869. Which statement about the pericardium is correct: the transverse pericardial sinus lies behind the aorta and the pulmonary trunk, the oblique sinus lies in front of the aorta, the fibrous pericardium is the serous layer, or the visceral layer lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium? The answer is that the transverse sinus lies behind those two vessels. The oblique sinus lies behind the left atrium.

Question 8870. Which vein drains the right posterior intercostal spaces and the right side of the back, and empties into the superior vena cava? The answer is the azygos vein. It begins in the abdomen and ascends on the right of the vertebral column. It arches over the root of the right lung to join the superior vena cava.

Question 8871. A described chest radiograph shows the windpipe dividing into two branches, the left one running more horizontally than the right. Why is the left main bronchus more horizontal? The answer is that the arch of the aorta passes over it. The right main bronchus is wider and more vertical, so an inhaled object lodges there more often.

Question 8872. Which of these pairs belongs together: the right ventricle with the pulmonary trunk, the left ventricle with the pulmonary trunk, the right atrium with the aorta, or the left atrium with the superior vena cava? The answer is the right ventricle with the pulmonary trunk. The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, and the left ventricle pumps it into the aorta.

Question 8873. Which chamber of the heart lies immediately behind the sternum and forms most of the front of the heart: the right atrium, the right ventricle, the left ventricle, or the left atrium? The answer is the right ventricle. It lies behind the lower sternum and the costal cartilages. The right atrium forms the right border of the heart.

Question 8874. Which vein lies immediately to the right of the thoracic duct in the posterior mediastinum and receives the hemiazygos vein? The answer is the azygos vein. The hemiazygos vein ascends on the left and crosses the vertebral column to join it. The thoracic duct ascends between the aorta and the azygos vein.

Question 8875. Which nerve descends behind the root of the lung, forms a plexus on the back of the esophagus and continues to the abdomen? The answer is the vagus nerve. Its branches intertwine around the esophagus to form the esophageal plexus. They pass through the diaphragm beside the esophagus.

Question 8876. True or false: the apex of each lung rises above the level of the medial third of the clavicle. The answer is true. The apex reaches about 2 to 3 centimeters above that point. It is covered by the cervical pleura, which is reinforced above by a membrane.

Question 8877. Which of these structures is found in the right atrium: the fossa ovalis, the moderator band, the papillary muscles, or the aortic vestibule? The answer is the fossa ovalis. It is the remnant of the opening between the two atria in the fetus. The moderator band and the papillary muscles belong to the ventricles.

Question 8878. A constructed illustration: blood collects rapidly in the sac around the heart, and the chambers cannot fill. Which space holds the blood, and which two layers bound it? The answer is the pericardial cavity, between the fibrous pericardium and the serous layer on the heart. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8879. Which large artery leaves the left ventricle, arches backward to the left, and then descends through the chest to the abdomen? The answer is the aorta. Its first part is the ascending aorta, hidden behind the pulmonary trunk. The arch gives off the arteries to the head, the neck and the upper limbs.

Question 8880. A described specimen of the heart is opened and shows a chamber with ridges on its inner wall and a band of muscle crossing from the wall between the ventricles to the front wall. Which chamber and which band are described? The answer is the right ventricle and the moderator band. The band carries part of the conducting system.

Question 8881. Which statement about the coronary arteries is correct: the right coronary artery supplies the right atrium and the right ventricle, the circumflex artery arises from the right coronary artery, the anterior interventricular artery from the right coronary artery, or the posterior interventricular artery from the left coronary artery? The answer is the first statement. In most people the posterior interventricular artery comes from the right coronary artery.

Question 8882. The heart lies in the middle of the chest with its long axis running downward, forward and left. In which plane does that axis lie, and on which side of the midline is the apex? The answer is an oblique plane, and the apex lies to the left of the midline. A cut in the plane of the long axis shows all four chambers.

Question 8883. Which plane divides the mediastinum into a superior and an inferior part, and between which two landmarks is it drawn? The answer is the transverse thoracic plane, drawn from the sternal angle back to the lower border of the fourth thoracic vertebra. The superior mediastinum lies above it, and the inferior mediastinum below.

Question 8884. Which statement about an intercostal space is correct: the vein, the artery and the nerve lie in the groove under the rib, in that order from above down, the nerve lies above the artery, the artery lies above the vein, or all three lie deep to the lining of the chest? The answer is the first statement. The bundle is protected by the lower border of the rib above it.

Question 8885. Which structure lies in the costal groove under a rib, deepest of the three that run there, and can be injured by a needle passed just above a rib? The answer is the intercostal nerve. The vein lies above it and the artery between them. A needle is therefore passed just above the lower rib of a space.

Question 8886. A constructed illustration: after a fall, a person struggles to breathe, the right side of the chest does not move, and tapping gives a hollow note. Which space has filled with air, and what has happened to the right lung? The answer is the right pleural cavity, with the lung collapsed. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8887. A described cross section of the chest shows the heart in the middle, a lung on each side, and a nerve running in front of the root of each lung. Which nerve is described, and what does it supply below? The answer is the phrenic nerve, which supplies the diaphragm. It also carries sensation from the pericardium and the mediastinal pleura.

Question 8888. Which of these pairs belongs together: the aortic opening of the diaphragm with the aorta, the caval opening with the esophagus, the esophageal opening with the inferior vena cava, or the aortic opening with the inferior vena cava? The answer is the aortic opening with the aorta. The caval opening carries the inferior vena cava, and the esophageal opening carries the esophagus and the vagus nerves.

Question 8889. Which structures pass through the esophageal opening of the diaphragm with the esophagus: the vagus nerves, the phrenic nerves, the thoracic duct, or the azygos vein? The answer is the vagus nerves, with the esophageal branches of the left gastric vessels. The opening lies at the level of the tenth thoracic vertebra, in the muscular part of the diaphragm.

Question 8890. Which muscle of the chest wall lies deepest of the three layers of the intercostal muscles and separates the space from the pleura? The answer is the innermost intercostal muscle. It is separated from the internal intercostal muscle by the vessels and nerve. Its fibers run in the same direction as the internal intercostal muscle.

Question 8891. Name two structures that lie in the middle mediastinum, spoken as a list. The answer is the heart with its pericardium, and the ascending aorta with the pulmonary trunk. The main bronchi and the phrenic nerves also lie in the middle mediastinum. That space lies at the level of the heart.

Question 8892. Which statement about the bronchopulmonary segments of the lung is correct: each has its own segmental bronchus and artery, the pulmonary veins run inside the segments, each lung has eight segments, or all the segments share one bronchus? The answer is that each segment has its own segmental bronchus and artery. The veins run between segments, which is why a segment can be removed.

Question 8893. A described chest radiograph shows a rounded shadow at the right cardiophrenic angle, and a side view shows it behind the lower sternum and in front of the heart. Which part of the mediastinum does it occupy? The answer is the anterior mediastinum. That space lies between the sternum and the pericardium, and it narrows toward the diaphragm.

Question 8894. Which structure ascends through the posterior mediastinum on the left of the vertebral column and ends at the junction of the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins? The answer is the thoracic duct. It begins in the abdomen as the cisterna chyli and passes through the aortic opening. It carries lymph from the whole body except the right upper quarter.

Question 8895. Which chamber of the heart receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins: the right atrium, the left atrium, the right ventricle, or the left ventricle? The answer is the left atrium. The four pulmonary veins open into its back wall. Blood then passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.

Question 8896. True or false: the visceral pleura covering the lung is insensitive to pain, while the parietal pleura lining the chest wall is sensitive. The answer is true. The parietal pleura is supplied by the intercostal and phrenic nerves, which carry pain. The visceral pleura has only autonomic nerves, so the lung feels no pain.

Question 8897. Which of these arteries is a branch of the right coronary artery in most people: the right marginal artery, the anterior interventricular artery, the circumflex artery, or the left marginal artery? The answer is the right marginal artery. The anterior interventricular and circumflex arteries are branches of the left coronary artery. The left marginal artery also comes from the left coronary artery.

Question 8898. A constructed illustration: a person is short of breath, the left side of the chest is dull when tapped, breath sounds are absent at the left base, and the windpipe stays in the midline. Which space is filled, and where does the fluid collect first? The answer is the left pleural cavity, with fluid first gathering in the costodiaphragmatic recess. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8899. A described specimen of the heart shows smooth inner surfaces in the two upper chambers and ridged surfaces in the two lower ones, and a probe passes through an opening between the upper chambers. Which opening is described? The answer is the fossa ovalis, the remnant of the foramen ovale. It lies between the right and the left atrium.

Question 8900. Which statement about the development of the diaphragm is correct: it is formed from the septum transversum, the pleuroperitoneal membranes, the dorsal mesentery of the esophagus and the body wall, it comes only from the septum transversum, it comes from the neural tube, or it comes from the neural crest? The answer is the first statement. The phrenic nerve reaches the diaphragm because it arises in the neck.

To summarize, the face is moved by the facial nerve and the jaws by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve, with the lateral pterygoid the only muscle of chewing that pulls the jaw forward, and the temporomandibular joint divided by a disc into a hinge and a gliding part. The parotid gland wraps around the ramus of the mandible with the facial nerve inside it, the submandibular gland lies in the floor of the mouth, and the tongue is moved by the hypoglossal nerve while its taste and its general sensation travel with other nerves. The neck is divided by the sternocleidomastoid muscle into two triangles, holds the carotid sheath with the carotid artery, the internal jugular vein and the vagus nerve, and carries the phrenic nerve on the front of the scalenus anterior. In the chest, the diaphragm separates the two cavities, and its three openings carry the inferior vena cava, the esophagus with the vagus nerves, and the aorta with the thoracic duct, while the right lung has three lobes and the left two. This chapter is educational material and does not replace an anatomy course, a dissection, a clinical training program, or the judgment of a teacher.

# Chapter 90 — Thorax, Part Two

This chapter continues the regional anatomy of the trunk, taking the thorax first and the abdomen second. The first half works through the mediastinum and its divisions, the heart and its coverings, the great vessels, the trachea and the bronchi, the lungs and the pleura, and the thoracic wall and the diaphragm. The second half follows the peritoneum and its folds, the foregut organs, the midgut and the hindgut, the posterior abdominal wall with its vessels, nerves and kidneys, the inguinal region, and the surface landmarks of the abdomen. It holds one hundred questions, and every one of them gives its answer immediately after the question and then explains why that answer is right, so nothing has to be held in mind until the end. The questions are written to be answered out loud from the relations of each structure rather than from a picture. This is educational material, and it supports rather than replaces an anatomy course, a dissection, a clinical training program, or the judgment of a teacher.

Question 8901. A described section of the chest is cut across the trunk through the disc between the fourth and fifth thoracic vertebrae. Which plane is this, and what does it separate? The answer is the transverse thoracic plane, which separates the superior mediastinum above from the inferior mediastinum below. The sternal angle marks it in front and the same disc marks it behind.

Question 8902. What name is given to the central compartment of the chest that lies between the two pleural cavities and holds the heart and the great vessels? The answer is the mediastinum. It extends from the superior thoracic aperture above to the diaphragm below. The lungs and their pleural coverings lie on either side of it.

Question 8903. Which part of the mediastinum contains the heart and the pericardium: the superior mediastinum, the anterior mediastinum, the middle mediastinum, or the posterior mediastinum? The answer is the middle mediastinum. It lies between the anterior mediastinum in front and the posterior mediastinum behind. The superior mediastinum lies above the heart.

Question 8904. Which subdivision of the mediastinum lies immediately behind the sternum and in front of the pericardium, and holds loose fat and, in the child, the thymus? The answer is the anterior mediastinum. It is the narrowest of the divisions. In the adult it holds little more than connective tissue.

Question 8905. Which structures lie in the posterior mediastinum, immediately in front of the bodies of the thoracic vertebrae? The answer is the esophagus, the descending thoracic aorta and the thoracic duct, with the azygos vein on the right. The esophagus lies against the vertebral column, and the thoracic duct runs behind it.

Question 8906. A described frontal radiograph of the chest shows the heart as a shadow in the middle of the thorax. Which chamber forms most of the right border of that shadow? The answer is the right atrium. The left ventricle forms the left border and the apex.

Question 8907. Which statement about the fibrous pericardium is correct: it is a single layer of serous membrane, a tough sac fused below to the central tendon of the diaphragm, the lining of the lungs, or the membrane that secretes pleural fluid? The answer is the tough sac fused below to the central tendon of the diaphragm. It is inelastic, so fluid collecting inside it can compress the heart.

Question 8908. What is the name of the smooth serous membrane that lines the inside of the fibrous pericardium and is reflected onto the surface of the heart? The answer is the serous pericardium. Its parietal layer lines the fibrous sac, and its visceral layer, the epicardium, covers the heart.

Question 8909. Which nerve runs downward in front of the root of the lung, between the fibrous pericardium and the mediastinal pleura, and supplies the diaphragm? The answer is the phrenic nerve. It is joined on its course by the pericardiophrenic vessels. The vagus nerve lies behind the root of the lung instead.

Question 8910. A constructed illustration: after a wound to the left side of the chest, the heart sounds become muffled and the neck veins are distended. Which space has filled with blood, and what limits its expansion? The answer is the pericardial cavity, limited by the tough fibrous pericardium, which prevents the heart from filling. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8911. The transverse pericardial sinus is a passage in the pericardial cavity. Between which structures does it lie: between the aorta and the pulmonary trunk in front and the superior vena cava behind, between the two atria, between the two ventricles, or between the heart and the lungs? The answer is between the aorta and the pulmonary trunk in front and the superior vena cava behind. A ligature passed through it controls the great vessels.

Question 8912. A described computed tomography section through the chest at the level of the heart shows the four chambers in one plane. Which chamber lies most anterior, immediately behind the sternum? The answer is the right ventricle. The right atrium lies to its right and the left atrium behind it.

Question 8913. True or false: the left atrium is the most posterior chamber of the heart and lies immediately in front of the esophagus. The answer is true. An enlarged left atrium can press on the esophagus and make swallowing difficult. On a described barium swallow the atrium makes a smooth impression on its front.

Question 8914. Which vein runs in the posterior part of the coronary sulcus, collects most of the blood from the heart muscle, and opens into the right atrium just above the opening of the inferior vena cava? The answer is the coronary sinus. The great cardiac vein is its largest tributary.

Question 8915. Which artery arises from the left aortic sinus, passes between the left atrium and the pulmonary trunk, and divides into the anterior interventricular and circumflex branches: the right coronary artery, the left coronary artery, the circumflex artery alone, or the posterior interventricular artery? The answer is the left coronary artery. The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the coronary sulcus.

Question 8916. Which structure lies immediately behind the manubrium and in front of the trachea, and is large in the child but regresses in the adult? The answer is the thymus. In the adult it is replaced largely by fat and connective tissue. It lies in the anterior part of the superior mediastinum.

Question 8917. Which of these pairs belongs together: the right atrium with the opening of the coronary sinus, the left atrium with the opening of the superior vena cava, the right ventricle with the mitral valve, or the left ventricle with the tricuspid valve? The answer is the right atrium with the opening of the coronary sinus. The mitral valve guards the left atrioventricular opening instead.

Question 8918. Which great vessel arises from the right ventricle and lies immediately in front of and to the left of the ascending aorta: the pulmonary trunk, the superior vena cava, the arch of the aorta, or the thoracic duct? The answer is the pulmonary trunk. It carries venous blood to the lungs.

Question 8919. A constructed illustration: a young person has high blood pressure in the arms and weak pulses in the legs. Which short segment of the aorta is narrowed, and which remnant marks the site? The answer is the aortic isthmus, just distal to the left subclavian artery, at the ligamentum arteriosum. Blood reaches the lower body through collateral channels.

Question 8920. Which fibrous remnant connects the left pulmonary artery to the under surface of the arch of the aorta, and which fetal vessel did it carry blood through? The answer is the ligamentum arteriosum, the remains of the ductus arteriosus. In the fetus that vessel carried blood from the pulmonary trunk to the aorta.

Question 8921. A described computed tomography image of the superior mediastinum shows a vessel arching over the right main bronchus and joining the superior vena cava. Which vein is described? The answer is the azygos vein. It ascends on the right of the vertebral column and drains the posterior intercostal veins.

Question 8922. How many branches arise from the arch of the aorta, and which one is given off first: one, the left subclavian artery; two, the left common carotid artery; three, the brachiocephalic trunk; or four, the right subclavian artery? The answer is three, the brachiocephalic trunk first. Then follow the left common carotid and the left subclavian arteries.

Question 8923. Which tube begins at the lower border of the larynx, lies in the midline of the neck and the superior mediastinum, and divides into two main bronchi? The answer is the trachea. It ends at the carina, at the level of the sternal angle. Its wall is reinforced by C-shaped rings of cartilage.

Question 8924. In the superior mediastinum, which structure lies immediately in front of the trachea, and which lies immediately behind it? The answer is the arch of the aorta in front and the esophagus behind. The arch crosses from right to left in front of the windpipe.

Question 8925. Name two structures that lie immediately in front of the trachea in the superior mediastinum. The answer is the arch of the aorta and the left brachiocephalic vein, with the thymus in front of both in the child. The brachiocephalic vein crosses the midline from left to right.

Question 8926. Which main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical, so that an inhaled foreign body is more likely to enter it: the right, the left, both equally, or the trachea itself? The answer is the right main bronchus. The left is longer and more horizontal because it passes under the arch of the aorta.

Question 8927. A described frontal radiograph of the chest shows a dark space in the lower left corner, with the lung edge retracted and the diaphragm blunted. Which space has filled with air? The answer is the pleural cavity, between the visceral and the parietal pleura. The two layers are normally held together by surface tension.

Question 8928. Which structure lies most posteriorly in the root of each lung, behind the pulmonary artery and the pulmonary veins? The answer is the main bronchus. On the right side the eparterial bronchus lies above the pulmonary artery. The bronchus is the most posterior structure of the root.

Question 8929. How many bronchopulmonary segments are usually found in the right lung and in the left: ten in each, ten on the right and eight or nine on the left, eight on the right and ten on the left, or twelve in each? The answer is ten on the right and eight or nine on the left. Each segment has its own bronchus and its own artery. The left lung loses one or two segments to the lingula.

Question 8930. A constructed illustration: after a fracture of a rib, a person has sudden pain and breathlessness, and the described radiograph shows the lung edge separated from the chest wall. Which space has filled with air, and what has been breached? The answer is the pleural cavity, breached through the parietal pleura and the chest wall, so that the lung recoils toward the hilum.

Question 8931. Which fissure of the lung runs obliquely from the upper part of the posterior border down to the lower part of the anterior border, and is present on both sides? The answer is the oblique fissure. It separates the upper from the lower lobe on the left, and the upper and middle from the lower lobe on the right.

Question 8932. Which pair belongs together: the right lung with two fissures, the left lung with three lobes, the horizontal fissure with the left lung, or the cardiac notch with the right lung? The answer is the right lung with two fissures, the oblique and the horizontal. The left lung has two lobes and no horizontal fissure.

Question 8933. The tongue-shaped projection of lung tissue that lies below the cardiac notch, and corresponds to the middle lobe of the other lung, is named what: the lingula, the eparterial bronchus, the apex, or the hilum? The answer is the lingula, which belongs to the upper lobe of the left lung. It is made of two bronchopulmonary segments.

Question 8934. A described computed tomography section of the chest at the level of the carina shows a dark air-filled tube dividing into two. Which structure lies immediately behind the carina and behind the left atrium? The answer is the esophagus. It runs down the posterior mediastinum in front of the descending aorta.

Question 8935. What is the name of the dome of pleura that rises above the medial third of the clavicle into the root of the neck, and is covered by a fibrous membrane? The answer is the cupola, or cervical pleura. The suprapleural membrane covers it, and the apex of the lung lies inside it.

Question 8936. Within an intercostal space, in what order do the intercostal vein, artery and nerve lie from above downward, and where do they run? The answer is vein, artery and nerve, in the costal groove on the under surface of the rib above. They are protected there from a needle passed above the rib below.

Question 8937. The internal thoracic artery descends behind the costal cartilages beside the sternum and ends by dividing into which two arteries: the superior epigastric and the musculophrenic, the inferior epigastric and the superficial epigastric, the pericardiophrenic and the phrenic, or the intercostal and the subcostal? The answer is the superior epigastric and the musculophrenic. It also gives pericardiophrenic and anterior intercostal branches.

Question 8938. A described frontal radiograph of the chest shows the right dome of the diaphragm higher than the left, with a dark space between the base of the lung and the diaphragm. What is the name of that space, and which layers of pleura bound it? The answer is the costodiaphragmatic recess, bounded by the costal pleura above and the diaphragmatic pleura below.

Question 8939. What is the name of the small gap between the costal and the sternal origins of the diaphragm, through which the superior epigastric vessels and lymphatics pass? The answer is the sternocostal triangle. It lies between the two muscular slips near the lower end of the sternum, and tissue can herniate through it.

Question 8940. Which structures pass through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm at the level of the twelfth thoracic vertebra: the aorta and the thoracic duct, the inferior vena cava, the esophagus and the vagus nerves, or the phrenic nerves? The answer is the aorta and the thoracic duct, with the azygos vein. The inferior vena cava has its own opening higher up.

Question 8941. A constructed illustration: a person has numbness along the inner border of the forearm and a pulse that weakens when the arm is raised above the head. Between which two structures does the lower trunk of the brachial plexus pass? The answer is between the first rib and the clavicle, over the first rib, where the subclavian vessels also cross.

Question 8942. A described computed tomography image of the chest shows a vein crossing the midline in front of the trachea, running from left to right to join another vein. Which vessel is described? The answer is the left brachiocephalic vein. It joins the right brachiocephalic vein to form the superior vena cava.

Question 8943. Which structure lies lateral to the bodies of the thoracic vertebrae, deep to the parietal pleura, and receives white and gray rami communicantes from the spinal nerves: the sympathetic trunk, the vagus nerve, the thoracic duct, or the azygos vein? The answer is the sympathetic trunk. It runs down the posterior chest wall in front of the heads of the ribs.

Question 8944. The opening for the inferior vena cava in the diaphragm lies at which vertebral level: the eighth thoracic, the tenth thoracic, the twelfth thoracic, or the fourth thoracic? The answer is the eighth thoracic. It lies in the central tendon. The esophageal opening is at the tenth level and the aortic hiatus at the twelfth.

Question 8945. True or false: the esophagus passes through the diaphragm at the level of the tenth thoracic vertebra, together with the two vagus nerves. The answer is true. The esophageal opening lies in the muscular part of the diaphragm. The vagus nerves re-form below it as the anterior and posterior vagal trunks.

Question 8946. Which of these pairs belongs together: the caval opening with the eighth thoracic vertebra, the aortic hiatus with the tenth thoracic vertebra, the esophageal opening with the twelfth thoracic vertebra, or the caval opening with the twelfth thoracic vertebra? The answer is the caval opening with the eighth thoracic vertebra. The esophageal opening lies at the tenth and the aortic hiatus at the twelfth.

Question 8947. Which of these ribs is a typical rib, sharing the same features as the third to the ninth: the first, the second, the sixth, or the eleventh? The answer is the sixth. A typical rib has a head, a neck and a tubercle, and its shaft is curved and twisted. The first and the eleventh are atypical.

Question 8948. A constructed illustration: a wound at the root of the neck on the left is followed by a raised left dome of the diaphragm on the described radiograph. Which nerve has been injured, and where does it lie within the chest? The answer is the left phrenic nerve, which runs in front of the root of the lung between the pericardium and the mediastinal pleura.

Question 8949. The recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around a different structure on each side. Which two: the left around the aortic arch and the right around the right subclavian artery, the left around the left subclavian artery and the right around the arch, both around the pulmonary arteries, or both around the carotid arteries? The answer is the left around the aortic arch and the right around the right subclavian artery, because the sixth aortic arch persists on the left.

Question 8950. A described radiograph of the chest shows the trachea pushed to the right, a dense white shadow filling the lower left chest, and the left border of the heart lost. What has collected in the pleural cavity? The answer is a large collection of fluid, which pushes the mediastinum toward the opposite side. Collapse of a lung pulls it toward the same side instead.

Question 8951. What is the name of the thin serous membrane that lines the wall of the abdominal cavity and covers the surfaces of the organs within it? The answer is the peritoneum. Its parietal layer lines the wall and its visceral layer covers the organs. The narrow space between them is the peritoneal cavity.

Question 8952. Which part of the peritoneal cavity lies behind the stomach and the lesser omentum, and communicates with the rest through a small opening: the greater sac, the lesser sac, the pleural cavity, or the retroperitoneal space? The answer is the lesser sac, also called the omental bursa. It communicates with the greater sac through the epiploic foramen.

Question 8953. Which structure forms the anterior boundary of the epiploic foramen, and which forms the posterior boundary? The answer is the free edge of the lesser omentum, containing the portal vein, in front, and the inferior vena cava behind. The foramen is the doorway between the greater and the lesser sac.

Question 8954. What is the name of the fan-shaped double layer of peritoneum that suspends the jejunum and the ileum from the posterior abdominal wall and carries their vessels? The answer is the mesentery. Its root runs obliquely from the left of the second lumbar vertebra to the right sacroiliac joint. It carries the superior mesenteric vessels.

Question 8955. A described computed tomography section of the upper abdomen shows a large organ on the right with vessels entering a deep transverse groove on its inferior surface. Which organ is shown, and what is the name of that groove? The answer is the liver, and the groove is the porta hepatis, through which the portal vein, the hepatic artery and the bile duct pass.

Question 8956. Which part of the stomach lies above the level of the cardiac opening, fills with gas when a person stands, and appears as a bubble on a described radiograph: the fundus, the body, the pyloric antrum, or the pyloric canal? The answer is the fundus, the highest part of the stomach, lying under the left dome of the diaphragm.

Question 8957. Which ring of smooth muscle guards the outlet of the stomach and controls the passage of its contents into the duodenum? The answer is the pyloric sphincter. It lies where the stomach joins the first part of the duodenum. Its thickened circular muscle forms a palpable ring.

Question 8958. A constructed illustration: a person has burning pain in the upper abdomen that wakes them at night, and the described radiograph shows a rounded projection from the first part of the duodenum. Which part of the gut is involved? The answer is the duodenal cap, the commonest site of a duodenal ulcer. The management belongs to the treating clinician and the local protocol.

Question 8959. The greater curvature of the stomach is supplied by which pair of arteries: the right and left gastric arteries, the right and left gastroepiploic arteries, the short gastric and the left gastric arteries, or the splenic and the hepatic arteries alone? The answer is the right and left gastroepiploic arteries, which join one another along the curvature. The gastric arteries run along the lesser curvature.

Question 8960. Which large vessels lie immediately behind the third part of the duodenum as it crosses the midline from right to left? The answer is the abdominal aorta and the inferior vena cava. The third part also crosses in front of the right ureter and the psoas muscle. The superior mesenteric artery crosses in front of the duodenum above it.

Question 8961. Which part of the pancreas lies immediately in front of the portal vein, is grooved by the superior mesenteric vessels, and joins the head to the body? The answer is the neck of the pancreas. It lies in front of the portal vein, which is formed behind it. The uncinate process hooks behind the superior mesenteric vessels.

Question 8962. A described section of the upper abdomen shows a long gland lying across the midline in front of two large vessels, with its tail reaching an organ on the left. Which gland is shown? The answer is the pancreas, whose tail reaches the spleen at its hilum. The gland lies behind the stomach.

Question 8963. True or false: the spleen lies in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen, between the fundus of the stomach and the left kidney, and its long axis follows the direction of the tenth rib. The answer is true. It lies below the left dome of the diaphragm, and it is covered by peritoneum except at its hilum.

Question 8964. Which lobe of the liver lies immediately to the left of the groove for the inferior vena cava and to the right of the fissure for the ligamentum venosum: the right lobe, the left lobe, the caudate lobe, or the quadrate lobe? The answer is the caudate lobe, on the posterior part of the inferior surface. The quadrate lobe lies further forward, between the gallbladder and the round ligament.

Question 8965. What is the name of the transverse fissure on the inferior surface of the liver through which the portal vein, the hepatic artery and the bile duct enter and leave? The answer is the porta hepatis. It lies between the caudate lobe behind and the quadrate lobe in front. All the vessels and ducts of the liver pass through it.

Question 8966. In which direction does the long axis of each kidney run, and which pole lies nearer the midline? The answer is that the long axis runs downward and laterally, so the upper pole lies nearer the midline. The right kidney lies a little lower than the left because the liver lies above it.

Question 8967. From the surface inward, which is the correct order of the coverings of the kidney: renal fascia, fat, fibrous capsule; fibrous capsule, fat, renal fascia; fat, fibrous capsule, renal fascia; or renal fascia, fibrous capsule, fat? The answer is renal fascia, then fat, then the fibrous capsule, which lies directly on the organ.

Question 8968. Which organs lie immediately in front of the right kidney, and which gland caps its upper pole? The answer is the liver above, with the second part of the duodenum and the ascending colon lower down, and the right adrenal gland capping the upper pole. The peritoneum covers the front of the kidney.

Question 8969. What is the name of the muscular tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder and crosses in front of the psoas muscle? The answer is the ureter. It begins at the hilum of the kidney and runs downward and medially on the posterior abdominal wall. It crosses the pelvic brim in front of the common iliac artery.

Question 8970. A described radiograph of the abdomen shows a narrow tube running down from the hilum of each kidney, crossing the tips of the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae before turning into the pelvis. Which structure is shown? The answer is the ureter. It lies in front of the psoas muscle and behind the peritoneum, and it narrows at three points.

Question 8971. Which pair belongs together: the superior mesenteric artery with the foregut, the inferior mesenteric artery with the hindgut, the celiac trunk with the midgut, or the inferior mesenteric artery with the foregut? The answer is the inferior mesenteric artery with the hindgut, from the distal transverse colon to the upper rectum. The celiac trunk supplies the foregut.

Question 8972. Which three arteries arise from the celiac trunk: the left gastric, the splenic and the common hepatic; the superior mesenteric, the inferior mesenteric and the splenic; the right gastric, the right gastroepiploic and the gastroduodenal; or the phrenic, the suprarenal and the renal? The answer is the left gastric, the splenic and the common hepatic. They supply the foregut.

Question 8973. Which blind tube arises from the posteromedial aspect of the cecum, below the junction with the ileum, and is suspended by a small mesentery containing its artery? The answer is the vermiform appendix. Its base lies at the meeting point of the three taeniae of the cecum. Its position varies, and it is retrocecal in many people.

Question 8974. Which structure lies immediately above and lateral to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, and into which canal does it open? The answer is the deep inguinal ring, which opens into the inguinal canal. The inferior epigastric artery lies medial to it and separates it from the superficial ring.

Question 8975. Name the three structures that pass through the porta hepatis. The answer is the portal vein, the proper hepatic artery and the hepatic ducts. The portal vein lies behind the other two. They are wrapped together in the free edge of the lesser omentum.

Question 8976. Blood from the abdominal part of the digestive tract, the spleen and the pancreas reaches the liver by which vein: the portal vein, the inferior vena cava, the hepatic veins, or the azygos vein? The answer is the portal vein, which carries blood rich in absorbed nutrients to the liver. The blood then leaves by the hepatic veins.

Question 8977. A described section of the upper abdomen shows a large vein running upward behind the neck of the pancreas, formed where two tributaries join. Which vein is described, and where does it end? The answer is the portal vein, formed by the splenic and the superior mesenteric veins, and it ends at the porta hepatis.

Question 8978. A constructed illustration: a swelling in the groin descends into the scrotum when the person coughs. Through which two openings does it pass, and which artery lies medial to the second of them? The answer is the deep inguinal ring and then the superficial inguinal ring, with the inferior epigastric artery medial to the deep ring.

Question 8979. What is the name of the passage about 4 centimeters long that runs obliquely through the lower part of the anterior abdominal wall, from the deep ring to the superficial ring? The answer is the inguinal canal. In the male it transmits the spermatic cord and in the female the round ligament of the uterus.

Question 8980. The anterior wall of the inguinal canal is formed mainly by which structure: the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle, the internal oblique muscle, the transversus abdominis muscle, or the rectus abdominis muscle? The answer is the aponeurosis of the external oblique. The internal oblique reinforces the lateral part of that wall.

Question 8981. True or false: the femoral canal lies medial to the femoral vein and is the site at which a femoral hernia appears. The answer is true. The canal is the small medial compartment of the femoral sheath, and it contains a lymph node. It is wider in women, so a femoral hernia is commoner in them.

Question 8982. Which pair belongs together: the ileum with abundant lymphoid aggregates, the jejunum with abundant lymphoid aggregates, the ileum with thick prominent circular folds, or the jejunum with a wall that is thin and poorly supplied with blood? The answer is the ileum with abundant lymphoid aggregates, the Peyer patches. The jejunum has the thicker wall and the taller folds.

Question 8983. Which part of the large intestine lies behind the peritoneum and has no mesentery of its own: the transverse colon, the sigmoid colon, the ascending colon, or the appendix? The answer is the ascending colon. The transverse and sigmoid parts have mesenteries and are mobile. The ascending part lies against the posterior abdominal wall.

Question 8984. What name is given to the three narrow bands of longitudinal muscle that run along the wall of the colon and gather at the base of the appendix? The answer is the taeniae coli. The sacculations between them are the haustra. The fatty tags along the colon are the appendices epiploicae.

Question 8985. A described computed tomography scan of the abdomen shows a thick-walled loop of bowel in the left iliac fossa, with fat inflammation around it and small pouches along its wall.
